newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's president strongly urges tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's president strongly urges tax reforms.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament must push through tax reforms if the former Soviet republic hopes to achieve financial stability, President Leonid Kuchma said during his yearly address to the nation on Friday.
"We need deep tax reforms," Kuchma said to parliamentarians and members of his government during the hour and a half speech.
Parliament is reviewing a package of nine new tax laws, which will underpin the much-delayed 1997 budget.
The budget would pave the way for receipt of a three-year $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility credit from the International Monetary Fund.
Kuchma said tax reform included lowering pressure on small- and medium-sized businesses.

Ukraine's unwieldy tax system, unreformed since the country gained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, heavily penalises those individuals and businesses who have not escaped into the shadow economy -- now estimated to take up half of all economic activity.
Kuchma said almost 11,000 state-run businesses in the natural resource sector, like gas, oil, electricity, metal, chemical, sugar and alcohol, are freed from paying taxes under current laws.
"Calculations show that if these enterprises paid their dues to the budget we would have no problems with pensions or wages."
Ukraine's wage debt to its workers is 4.2 billion hryvnias, and the pension fund owes 1.1 billion hryvnias.
Kuchma said once the tax reform package is accepted, there would be a moratorium on changes to tax laws to 1999.
"Financial stability is possible only with realistic revenues and expenditures in the budget," the president said.
